correctness.rationale: Every labelled complete-bipartite four-color update factors exactly through 225 nonempty ordered color supports. Recurrence conserves both support cardinalities and makes per-step maps bijective on represented colors, so every surjective assignment has the induced period. A standalone deterministic exhaustive 225-mask support graph and return-permutation checker establishes exactly 25 periodic support pairs with periods 1/4/6, and surjection inclusion–exclusion proves the formulas for every positive shore size. An independent full-state implementation exhaustively verifies 115600 labelled states for all 1<=a,b<=4. Finite labelled tests are corroboration, not the infinite-family proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches for four-color cyclic successor-contact automata and six-cycle censuses, comparisons against closest mathematical records and earlier three-color biclique results, and material inspection of primary works find no equivalent theorem or stronger result that entails all three labelled population formulas. Four-color spirals and long periods on other graphs are known and not claimed as novel. Unindexed equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently titled source could already contain an equivalent four-color complete-bipartite census.

Finite 225-state support table is exact only conditional on independent scrutiny of the embedded deterministic enumeration; it is not a human-only derivation of each table entry.

value.rationale: The first cyclic palette beyond three colors exhibits an exact primitive six-cycle stratum, sharp two-shore size thresholds, a disjoint all-color four-cycle stratum and complete population formulas in surjection counts. This infinite-family result is motivated by the documented higher-color complication of cyclic graph dynamics; it classifies true dynamical recurrent populations, not a routine algebra substitution or arbitrary numerical slice.
